facts.fact: European powers build rival military alliances before 1914, splitting Europe into two armed camps.
facts.note: Standard account of the alliance system.

facts.fact: Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy initially form the Triple Alliance in 1882.
facts.note: The alliance was signed in May 1882. Italy stayed neutral in 1914 and joined the Allies in 1915. The brief omits this.

facts.fact: Great Britain, France, and Russia counter by forming the Triple Entente in 1907.
facts.note: The Anglo-Russian Entente of 1907 completed it. It was an entente, not a formal alliance. The brief leaves out the 1894 Franco-Russian alliance and the 1904 Entente Cordiale.

facts.fact: Imperial competition for overseas colonies increases tension and fuels naval arms races among these powers.
facts.note: Broadly accepted, but vague. The Anglo-German naval race is the main case and is not named. Colonial rivalry is also debated as a cause.

facts.fact: Nationalist movements in the Balkan region create intense political instability inside the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
facts.note: Vague. It omits the 1908 annexation of Bosnia and the Balkan Wars of 1912-13.

facts.fact: On June 28, 1914, a Serbian nationalist assassinates Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo.
facts.note: Gavrilo Princip was a Bosnian Serb, a Young Bosnia member. Calling him a Serbian nationalist is acceptable but imprecise. He is not named.

facts.fact: Austria-Hungary blames Serbia for the assassination and declares war on July 28, 1914.
facts.note: The July Ultimatum of 23 July and Germany's 'blank cheque' are missing.

facts.fact: Russia mobilizes its army to defend Serbia against Austria-Hungary.
facts.note: Russia began general mobilization on 30-31 July. No date is given.

facts.fact: Germany backs Austria-Hungary and declares war on Russia and France in August 1914.
facts.note: Germany declared war on Russia on 1 Aug and on France on 3 Aug. The Schlieffen Plan is missing.

facts.fact: Great Britain enters the war after German forces invade neutral Belgium.
facts.note: Britain declared war on 4 Aug 1914. The 1839 Treaty of London guaranteed Belgian neutrality.

facts.fact: The war causes the collapse of four major imperial dynasties: Russian, German, Austro-Hungarian, and Ottoman.
facts.note: The Romanov, Hohenzollern, Habsburg and Ottoman dynasties all fell. The Ottoman sultanate was abolished in 1922.

facts.fact: The Russian Empire falls to the Bolshevik Revolution in 1917, establishing Soviet rule.
facts.note: The tsar abdicated in the February 1917 revolution. The Bolsheviks seized power in October 1917. The brief makes the monarchy's fall look like the Bolshevik act. The USSR was formally founded in 1922.

facts.fact: Austria-Hungary fractures into several independent nation-states, including Austria, Hungary, and Czechoslovakia.
facts.note: Yugoslavia, in its Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes form, and parts of Poland and Romania also took its lands.

facts.fact: The 1919 Treaty of Versailles imposes heavy financial reparations and territorial losses on Germany.
facts.note: The war guilt clause, military limits and the 132 billion gold mark figure of 1921 are missing.

facts.fact: Allied diplomats divide former Ottoman lands across the Middle East into British and French mandates.
facts.note: The mandates were Iraq, Palestine and Transjordan (British) and Syria and Lebanon (French). The Sykes-Picot agreement and San Remo (1920) are not named.

facts.fact: The peace treaties establish the League of Nations to prevent future international conflicts.
facts.note: The League was created by the Covenant in the Versailles treaty in 1920. The US never joined. This is a key weakness and is not mentioned.

facts.fact: The conflict causes an estimated 15 to 22 million military and civilian deaths worldwide.
facts.note: Common estimates range from about 15 to 22 million, with roughly 9-10 million military deaths. The range is wide and unsourced.

facts.fact: Economic disruption and unresolved territorial grievances from the war set the stage for World War II.
facts.note: A common view. It is stated without detail such as hyperinflation, the Depression or the rise of Nazism.
